scope: Full scope over the 8 synthetic_reference artifacts named in reviewed_ids: the project scope FB2-MAN-SCO-000001, the safety plan FB2-MAN-SPL-000001, the HSI design FB2-SYS-HSI-000001, and the five scenario fixtures FB2-SCN-MUT-000001..000002 and FB2-SCN-CHG-000001..000003. This is a complete review of these 8 artifacts and is not a sample. The remaining 18 mutation scenarios and the remaining scenario expectations are outside this record's scope and are explicitly not claimed to have been reviewed.

findings.description: The project scope, the safety plan and the HSI design each carry an empty source_refs array. For the scope and the safety plan this is defensible: both are planning artifacts whose content is a statement of intent about a hypothetical project, and inventing an anchor for them would be worse than having none. For the HSI design it is a genuine weakness: FB2-SYS-HSI-000001 does carry three source anchors (FB2-SRC-COD-000001, FB2-SRC-COD-000004, FB2-SRC-HW-000002), but it specifies electrical budgets, timing budgets, fault indications and interface signal levels in detail and cites no anchor for any of them individually. A reader cannot tell which stated budgets are derived from source and which are synthetic. Recorded as a provenance-granularity finding, not as an ungrounded artifact.
findings.evidence: FB2-MAN-SCO-000001 source_refs [], FB2-MAN-SPL-000001 source_refs [], both lifecycle_status 'baselined' with no provenance. FB2-SYS-HSI-000001 source_refs ['FB2-SRC-COD-000001', 'FB2-SRC-COD-000004', 'FB2-SRC-HW-000002'] at artifact level only; its interfaces, electrical_budgets, timing_budget and fault_indications blocks carry no per-item source_refs.

findings.description: The two mutation fixtures carried in the artifact index declare their expected detector, expected finding (with severity, category and description) and expected remediation inside the ingestible artifact itself, which is the answer-leakage pattern the master prompt warns against: expected labels belong in a separate evaluator manifest so a checker cannot pass by reading the answer. This is checked and recorded as an observation about corpus structure, not as a claim that the acceptance gate is compromised: the gate in corpus.py compares produced findings against expectations it derives from these records, and the records carry human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false. Whether the separation the master prompt asks for is adequately implemented is a question for the corpus owner; this review does not resolve it and made no change.
findings.evidence: FB2-SCN-MUT-000001 carries expected_detector 'traceability_checker', expected_finding {finding_id: FB2-FND-MUT-000001, severity: high, category: traceability, description: 'FSR has no parent safety goal (missing refines link)'} and expected_remediation. FB2-SCN-MUT-000002 carries the equivalent fields for the link_forbidden_relation_type detector. Both values were corrected on 2026-10-03 when the duplicate revision-1 copies these fixtures were removed from docs/artifacts/corpus/scenarios/; the text they replaced is preserved verbatim in this record's limitations array, entry beginning 'FB2-REV-FND-000152 evidence superseded on 2026-10-03'.

dispositions.action: Partially accepted. The empty provenance on the scope and the safety plan is correct for planning artifacts and needs no action. The artifact-level-only provenance on the HSI design is accepted as a real granularity weakness and is referred to the design owner. No artifact was edited; the design is outside this review's authoring scope.

Referred to the corpus owner as a structural question about where mutation expectations live. This review made no change to the scenario files, which are outside its write scope in any case, and did not weaken or alter any acceptance gate.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every artifact covered by this review. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit.

Scope is 8 artifacts, named individually. The corpus holds 20 mutation scenarios and 3 change lifecycles; only 2 mutation fixtures and all 3 change-lifecycle fixtures reachable through the artifact index were reviewed here. The remaining 18 mutation scenarios were NOT reviewed and no claim is made about them.

Verification performed: (a) provenance field presence and granularity read in all three planning/design artifacts; (b) the HSI design searched for any reference to the security requirement set, which produced FB2-REV-FND-000111 in FB2-REV-000003 and is cross-referenced here; (c) expected-label placement inspected in both mutation fixtures; (d) policy fields checked. (b) and (d) were clean.
The HSI design's interface signals, timing budget and electrical budgets were NOT re-derived against the real hardware. No board, schematic or hardware file was opened.
The scenario fixtures were read only. docs/artifacts/scenarios/change-lifecycles/*.json were not modified by this review or by any part of this pass.

FB2-REV-FND-000152 evidence superseded on 2026-10-03 (duplicate scenario fixture removal). Previous evidence text, preserved verbatim: FB2-SCN-MUT-000001 carries expected_detector 'Traceability completeness checker (missing parent)', expected_finding {finding_id: FB2-FND-MUT-000001, severity: high, category: traceability, description: 'FSR FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 has no parent safety goal (missing refines link)'} and expected_remediation. FB2-SCN-MUT-000002 carries the equivalent fields for the invalid-link-type detector. Reason: This evidence quoted expected_detector and expected_finding.description from the revision-1 copy of FB2-SCN-MUT-000001 that sat under docs/artifacts/corpus/scenarios/. That copy was removed on 2026-10-03; the surviving fixture at docs/artifacts/scenarios/mutations/mutation-001-missing-parent-link.json carries expected_detector 'traceability_checker' and the description 'FSR has no parent safety goal (missing refines link)', because it advanced to revision 2 on 2026-09-29. Quoting the removed copy would have left this record asserting a value that exists nowhere in the corpus. Only the quoted VALUES were corrected; the finding itself is unchanged, because the substance it reports -- expected labels declared inline in the ingestible artefact -- holds for the revision-2 fixture exactly as it held for revision 1. The revision-2 fixture is in fact stronger evidence for the finding than revision 1 was, since it also carries the evaluator-only oracle manifest at scenarios/evaluator-only/SCN-MUT-001/oracle-manifest.json that this finding says is what the inline declarations duplicate.
review_method: Field-level provenance inspection and a recursive substring search of the design artifact for cross-set references, plus structural inspection of the scenario fixtures for expectation placement.

This fixture existed twice under one id. The copy the artifact index resolved to sat at docs/artifacts/corpus/scenarios/mutations/ at revision 1; the copy the mutation harness executed sat at docs/artifacts/scenarios/mutations/ at revision 2. The review recorded the digest of the revision-1 copy, because the index -- the reader the review used to locate artefacts -- resolved to it. The revision-1 copy has been removed and the index now walks docs/artifacts/scenarios/, so the same id names one file and the harness and the index read the same bytes. The artefact itself advanced from revision 1 to revision 2 on 2026-09-29 (commit 566d6a41), which replaced the free-text expected_detector 'Traceability completeness checker (missing parent)' with the rule id 'traceability_checker' and restated the expected description as the message that rule emits. No finding, disposition, scope item or checklist entry of this review is added, withdrawn or altered, and the finding FB2-REV-FND-000152 is unchanged in substance: the revision-2 fixture still declares expected_detector, expected_finding and expected_remediation inline. The quoted expected_detector in that finding's evidence has been corrected to the current value with the superseded text preserved here. Re-issuing the digest asserts only that the digest matches the file as it now stands; this session did not re-examine the fixture.

Same duplicate-fixture removal as FB2-SCN-MUT-000001, for the invalid-relation_type mutation. The index resolved to a revision-1 copy under docs/artifacts/corpus/scenarios/mutations/; the harness executed the revision-2 copy under docs/artifacts/scenarios/mutations/, last modified 2026-09-29 in commit 566d6a41, which replaced the free-text expected_detector 'Link type validator (invalid relation_type)' with the rule id 'link_forbidden_relation_type' and restated the expected description. The revision-1 copy is removed. No finding, disposition, scope item or checklist entry of this review is added, withdrawn or altered, and this session did not re-examine the fixture.

Both copies claimed revision 1, so the revision field could not order them and content decided. The stale copy asserted 'FB2-LNK-SAF-000009 (test verifies)'; the link registry records FB2-LNK-SAF-000009 as allocated_to FB2-SW-SWR-000002 -> FB2-SAF-FSR-000002, and FB2-LNK-SAF-000014 as the verifies link. The stale copy therefore attributed a relation type to a link that does not have it, and omitted a suspect_links entry the live copy carries. The live copy is the accurate one and the stale copy has been removed. This is a bytes-replaced correction, not a revision advance: the artefact is still revision 1.

Both copies claimed revision 1. The live copy names the affected link as 'FB2-LNK-SAF-000011 (Design implements SWR-001)' where the stale copy read '(Design implements SWR)', and its risk_assessment adds the FMEDA / new-SW-architecture / new-verification consequence the stale copy omits. The one string the stale copy carried and the live copy did not -- the expanded source-anchor reference 'FB2-SRC-COD-000001/000002' against the live copy's abbreviated 'FB2-SRC-COD-000001/002' -- has been written into the live copy, which is why this artefact advanced to revision 2: the abbreviation matched the reference checker as a single id and silently covered only one of the two drivers the entry claims, while both FB2-SRC-COD-000001 and FB2-SRC-COD-000002 exist in the source registry. The stale copy has been removed. No finding, disposition, scope item or checklist entry of this review is added, withdrawn or altered, and this session did not re-examine the change record.
